_comment: Cross-language classification matrix for conf.d ENTRY NAMES (#1537, the
#1911 family). One conf.d tree is read by several independent enumerators,
each with its own hand-written name rule. The ones that shaped this table
are listed below; the full set of consumers is whatever
`git grep -l confd_name_classification_matrix` names today:
Go     the threshold-exporter's production hot-reload walker (named
by role, not file: it has moved once, #1568, and is due to move
again); what it classifies is what /metrics serves. Its test
entry point is still called scanDirHierarchical
Go     components/tenant-api/internal/confd (TenantIDFromFile) - the
write plane's filename<->tenant-id mapping, and the source of the
live-tenant set federation orphan detection subtracts against
Python scripts/tools/_lib_confd (_is_config / iter_config_files) - the
single answer to 'what is in a conf.d directory' for the tools
Python scripts/tools/_lib_io (iter_yaml_files) - the FLAT reader
They disagreed. Measured on the tree that produced this file: a root-level
`upper.YAML` was READ by the exporter (source_file=upper.YAML, merged into
the effective config it serves), completely INVISIBLE to both Python
readers - iter_config_files did not yield it and unusable_config_paths did
not name it, so no report mentioned it at all - and REJECTED by tenant-api,
which therefore listed 1 of 2 tenants and, worse, left that live tenant out
of the orphan detector's known-tenant set, so its legitimate federation
artifacts were proposed for cleanup while the exporter served it.
⛔ NEITHER SIDE ASSERTS THE OTHER, and no side greps the other's source.
This repo measured (#1448 blind review) that a Python guard asserting
things about Go source text goes red on legitimate Go refactors and states
the OPPOSITE of the truth when it does; the cheapest way back to green was
to undo a correct refactor. So every reader asserts THIS table instead,
which makes their agreement transitive rather than claimed.
THE ROWS ARE NAMES CARRYING ORTHOGONAL PROPERTIES, not an expected file
list. A single expected-list column would be a lie here, because the
enumerators do not have the same scope: _lib_confd recurses and keeps `_`
files, _lib_io is flat and takes skip_reserved as a parameter, tenant-api
is per-name and drops both prefixes, and the exporter routes `_defaults.*`
to the inheritance chain instead of treating it as a tenant carrier. Each
consumer asserts only the PROJECTION it actually implements:
_lib_confd._is_config          == yaml_extension AND NOT hidden
_lib_io.iter_yaml_files(True)  == yaml_extension AND NOT reserved_prefix
AND NOT hidden
_lib_io.iter_yaml_files(False) == yaml_extension          (the parameter
gates BOTH prefixes, so dotfiles come
back too - measured, not assumed)
confd.TenantIDFromFile ok      == yaml_extension AND NOT reserved_prefix
AND NOT hidden;  id == stem
scanDirHierarchical hashes     == yaml_extension AND NOT hidden
scanDirHierarchical defaults   == defaults_file
scanDirHierarchical tenants    == yaml_extension AND NOT reserved_prefix
AND NOT hidden  (fixture holds CONTENT
constant - every file is one valid
single-tenant document - so only the
NAME varies)
Property definitions, so a new row cannot be filled in by guesswork:
yaml_extension  - name lowercased ends with '.yaml' or '.yml'
reserved_prefix - name starts with '_' (platform control file)
hidden          - name starts with '.'
defaults_file   - name lowercased is exactly '_defaults.yaml' or
'_defaults.yml'; implies reserved_prefix AND
yaml_extension, and the consumers check that implication.
LOWERCASED, not case-FOLDED: the two relations differ
on U+017F (see the _defaultſ rows, #1670)
stem            - the tenant id the write plane derives from the name:
the name minus its extension, WITH THE STEM'S ORIGINAL
CASE PRESERVED (MiXeD.YmL -> MiXeD, never mixed).
Empty string when the name is not a tenant carrier.
⚠️ Rows that differ only by case (_defaults.yaml / _DEFAULTS.YAML,
.hidden.yaml / .HIDDEN.YAML, and _defaults.yaml / _defaultſ.yaml where
the filesystem folds U+017F) cannot all be materialised on a
case-insensitive filesystem. The two filesystem-backed consumers detect
that and SKIP with a message saying so; the pure-predicate consumers run
everywhere. 'Could not measure here' and 'measured and fine' are different
outcomes and are reported differently.

rows.name: db-a.yaml
rows.why: The ordinary case. If this row ever disagrees, the matrix is not describing conf.d at all.

rows.name: db-b.yml
rows.why: Both spellings ship; the .yml branch is a separate code path in every reader.

rows.name: tenant_123.yaml
rows.why: A mid-string underscore must NOT trip the reserved-prefix rule. Pins that reserved is a PREFIX test, not a contains test.

rows.name: upper.YAML
rows.why: ⛔ THE #1537 ROW. The exporter reads it and serves it. Before this change the two Python readers could not see it and tenant-api rejected it, which also dropped it from the orphan detector's live-tenant set.

rows.name: upshort.YML
rows.why: The .yml half of the same defect. A fix that only folds the .yaml branch leaves this one broken, and every reader has two branches.

rows.name: MiXeD.YmL
rows.why: ⛔ PINS THE ID DECISION. Mixed case both in the extension (must be folded) and in the stem (must NOT be). Deriving the id from the lowercased copy would silently rename this tenant to `mixed` on the write plane while the exporter keeps calling it whatever its `tenants:` key says — a second divergence built by the fix for the first.

rows.name: MiXeD2.Yaml
rows.why: ⛔ THE SECOND HALF OF THE ID PIN, and it is here because the dogfood run needed it: with a mixed-case stem only on the .yml row, corrupting the .yaml branch of the id derivation ALONE went undetected — every .yaml row happened to have an all-lowercase stem. Each extension branch needs its own mixed-stem row, and the anti-truncation floors demand both. Title-case extension is also the spelling an editor or a Windows tool produces by itself.

rows.name: İ.yaml
rows.why: stem offset must come from the CONSTANT's length, never from the folded copy: 'İ'.lower() is TWO characters (i + combining dot), so len(name.lower()) - len('.yaml') slices this name one position too far right and yields 'İ.'. Measured: with only same-length rows in this table that bug was invisible — every consumer stayed green.

rows.name: _defaults.yaml
rows.why: The inheritance chain's carrier (ADR-016/017). Reserved, so no plane may address it as a tenant, yet the exporter must still hash it and route it into the defaults chain.

rows.name: _DEFAULTS.YAML
rows.why: The uppercase spelling of the chain carrier. The exporter's walker CLASSIFIES by the lowercased name, so this is a carrier. ⛔ Until #1674 (B8) that was all it was: the exporter's inheritance chain matched only the two exact lower-case literals, so this file was hashed, entered in the walker's defaults set, and then left out of every tenant's chain — the exact 'hash it and quietly drop its `defaults:` block' failure this row used to attribute to a hypothetical reader, while /effective and describe_tenant did merge it. Since #1674 every chain picks one carrier per directory from the lowercased classification (a `.yaml` spelling beats `.yml`), so this file IS the chain level when it is the directory's carrier.

rows.name: _Defaults.Yml
rows.why: Mixed case across BOTH halves of the defaults name, and the .yml spelling of it — the combination that survives a fix applied to one branch only.

rows.name: _defaults-multidb.yaml
rows.why: a REAL file in this repo (conf.d/examples/) that starts with '_defaults' but is NOT the chain carrier: the exporter compares the lowercased name against the two literals exactly, so it never merges this into a tenant's chain. Without this row a PREFIX implementation of defaults_file passes every consumer - measured, it shipped briefly in #1588 and made describe_tenant reproduce the exporter's merged_hash on only 3 of 5 shipped tenants, and made deprecate_rule --execute write to this file.

rows.name: _defaultſ.yaml
rows.why: ⛔ THE FOLD-RELATION ROW (#1670). The last 's' is U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S. It is already lowercase, so lowercasing leaves it alone and the name is NOT the chain carrier - the exporter compares the lowercased name against the two literals. But Unicode simple case folding (Go strings.EqualFold, Python str.casefold) maps it to 's', so an implementation that folds instead of lowercasing calls it `_defaults.yaml`. Measured: Go's write plane did exactly that and routed this file into the Base PR as the chain carrier while the exporter merged none of its defaults: block. Every row other than these two gets the same defaults_file answer under both relations, so without them the two are indistinguishable.

rows.name: _defaultſ.yml
rows.why: The .yml half of the fold-relation row. The defaults comparison has one literal per extension and a fix applied to one of them leaves the other folding. Under SINGLE-rune substitution (every non-ASCII rune for each byte of the defaults literals) these two are the only names where the two relations disagree. Over every combination of each character's full fold orbit there are 3072 such names (e.g. `_DEFAULTſ.YAML`); all of them carry `ſ` in the `s` position, which is the character these two rows exercise.

rows.name: _rbac.yaml
rows.why: Reserved but NOT a defaults carrier. Separates the two reserved sub-cases: `_rbac.yaml` is hashed for change detection and skipped by everything else. A reader that collapsed reserved into defaults would pass every other row.

rows.name: _.yaml
rows.why: The degenerate reserved name. Its stem is empty, so any implementation that decides reserved-ness AFTER stripping the extension answers differently here.

rows.name: .hidden.yaml
rows.why: Hidden and YAML at once — the row that keeps `hidden` and `yaml_extension` from being conflated. It is the ONE row where _lib_io's two modes disagree with each other.

rows.name: .HIDDEN.YAML
rows.why: Case-folding must not resurrect a hidden file. A fix that folds the name and then tests the prefix on the folded copy still answers correctly here — but only because '.' has no case, which is itself measured in confd.isReservedName's note.

rows.name: .yaml
rows.why: A name that is nothing but the extension. Hidden wins. Pins that the extension test does not need a non-empty stem to fire, and that the hidden test is not skipped for short names.

rows.name: .gitkeep
rows.why: Hidden AND non-YAML — really present in shipping conf.d trees. Both reasons to skip apply, so a reader that lost one of them still passes; it is here so the property columns stay independent rather than as a detector on its own.

rows.name: README.md
rows.why: The ordinary non-YAML neighbour. Case folding must not turn the extension test into a substring test.

rows.name: noextension
rows.why: No dot at all. An implementation that split on '.' and inspected the last field would read the whole name as the extension.

rows.name: db-a.json
rows.why: A structured-config neighbour that is emphatically not conf.d input.

rows.name: db-a.yaml.bak
rows.why: ⛔ '.yaml' appears in the name but not at the end. The exact shape a customer produces by editing in place, and the one a `contains`-style test — or a fold done with a substring search — silently promotes back into the live config.

rows.name: yaml
rows.why: The extension without its dot. Pins that the suffix under test is '.yaml' and not 'yaml'.
